key_insight: Adjoint methods and PINNs are not universally superior; the best choice depends mainly on how the unknown is represented, with grid-based fields favoring adjoint optimization and neural representations favoring PINNs.
engineering_relevance: For PDE-constrained inverse problems in mechanics and flow, this study gives a fair apples-to-apples comparison that helps practitioners choose between accuracy, cost, and modeling flexibility.
method: Common abstract PDE inverse-problem setup for both methods
Matched domains, governing equations, observations, regularization, optimizer, parameterization, and precision
Benchmarked on Burgers, Darcy permeability, Allen–Cahn reaction ID, and Navier–Stokes viscosity ID
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates both approaches on multiple PDE inverse benchmarks under identical formulations and reports that representation choice strongly determines performance, with PINN warm-starting improving adjoint efficiency.
watch_item: Results depend on careful alignment of formulations and training settings; in practice, trajectory storage, differentiation cost, and parameterization choices can still shift which method is preferable.
paper_title: Adjoint Method versus Physics-Informed Neural Networks in PDE-Constrained Inverse Problems
